newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Pace of Easdaq listings set to hot up.
newsitem.headline: Pace of Easdaq listings set to hot up.

text.p: European small cap market Easdaq said on Thursday the pace of listings was due to hot up in coming weeks but it probably would not reach earlier expectations of 50 quotations by the end of 1997.
"Our view is that it's more likely to be 35 than 50 companies," a spokeswoman for the Brussels-based market, which launched last November and now has eight listings, told Reuters.
"However, there's quite a lot of momentum at the moment, so who knows," she added.
Belgian, Nasdaq-listed, speech technology firm Lernout & Hauspie on Wednesday became the latest company to say it would seek a quotation on Easdaq, which is modelled on the bigger U.S. market.
The listing, due to take place in June, would not involve the issue of any new shares, it said.
The Easdaq spokeswoman said around eight companies were likely to join the bourse before the summer.

"The market authority has approved six applications and we have another two pending which are likely to be approved. Of the eight, three are Easdaq IPOs, two are combined Easdaq/Nasdaq IPOs and three are dual listings," she said.

Easdaq chief executive officer Jacques Putzeys said in March the market still hoped to achieve 50 listings by the end of 1997. When it launched, Easdaq said it hoped to also tempt all 85 European companies listed on Nasdaq to seek a dual listing.
However, the market has found it difficult to find enough market makers willing to support dual listings. Each listing must be supported by at least two market makers.

"Despite 56 market makers liquidity is slightly disappointing...and is almost non-existent for companies listed on Nasdaq, with the exception of Dr Solomon's," Generale Bank head of corporate finance Marc-Antoine de Schoutheete told a recent conference.

De Schoutheete noted it was still early days for the market. The rival Euro.NM market in Paris, which targets slightly smaller companies with a less international outlook, took 12 months to gain a solid following, he said.
European companies listed on Easdaq say they are happy with the way the market is developing.

"We are satisfied with our listing," Artwork Systems co-founder Peter Lanoo told Reuters at the presentation of half year results earlier this week. "We are still confident that momentum will build but it's clear that it will take time."

Easdaq originated four years ago from contacts between the European Venture Capital Association, the European Commission and various market players. It is supported by Nasdaq, which is also one of its shareholders.
